primitives.name: Quality Index of Player
primitives.verbatim_quote: This paper tries to keep above two important aspects in mind and build a rating system called 'Quality Index of Player (φPlayer) which includes qualitative and quantitative aspects of player performance.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E(runs)': 'expected runs scored, dimensionless', '\\phi_{\\text{avg}}': 'average performance index, dimensionless', '\\sigma_{\\text{runs}}': 'standard deviation of runs, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Player performance is normally distributed; opposition strength affects run quality; dismissal value correlates with batsman average.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When opposition strength varies drastically or when sample size of matches is insufficient for stable estimates.

layer2.mapping: Maps raw performance metrics to normalized quality scores using statistical kernels derived from opponent ratings and career averages.

primitives.name: Player Embedding Space
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised statistical approach to build a team recommendation system for cricket by modelling players into embeddings.
primitives.assumptions: Players can be represented in a continuous vector space where proximity reflects similarity in role and performance traits.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player roles are ambiguous or when new players lack sufficient historical data for embedding generation.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphically maps player attributes to latent feature vectors that encode both individual and contextual performance.
layer2.telemetry: Cosine similarity between embedded player vectors across different match contexts.

primitives.name: Team Composition Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: We also embark on a critical aspect of team composition, which includes the number of batsmen and bowlers in the team.
primitives.assumptions: Optimal team balance requires fixed ratios of batsmen to bowlers based on match context and opposition profile.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When team composition deviates beyond allowable ranges or when match-specific strategies demand unconventional setups.

layer2.mapping: Enforces structural constraints on player embeddings to ensure valid team configurations during recommendation.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of valid team combinations generated under given constraints.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of CRICTRS lies in the synthesis of qualitative and quantitative metrics into a unified player embedding framework. The Quality Index of Player (φPlayer) serves as a foundational operator that adjusts raw statistics—like runs scored and wickets taken—by incorporating contextual elements such as opposition strength and career average. This adjustment ensures that a high score against a strong bowling attack is weighted more heavily than a similar score against a weak one. The embedding space is constructed using semi-supervised learning techniques, allowing the system to generalize from limited labeled data while leveraging rich unlabeled match histories. The team composition constraint enforces structural integrity by ensuring that recommended teams maintain balanced roles. These primitives interact through a dual mechanism: first, the φPlayer operator generates refined player profiles; second, these profiles are mapped into an embedding space where they undergo further optimization via constraint satisfaction. Failure modes arise when the assumption of normality breaks down due to sparse data or when opposition strength is misestimated, leading to skewed embeddings and suboptimal recommendations.
